body:
Reply with plain text only, no JSON, no preamble, and do not send messages to anyone else. Do not ask questions; decide.

You are drafting short Narrator lines for a Halloween D&D video game, "The Crooked Moon". The Narrator is the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of a ghost train, telling the tale afterwards in a folksy Southern drawl. This batch is set in the Crooked House, a haunted manor on a hill above the village of Wickermoor: a house that warps itself, built on old dark power. A storm has shut the party inside. Here the Vagrant's humour is gone. He is hushed, dry and dead level, the drawl stripped down to bare bones, with silences in it. Never a joke, never a gloat; the dead are respected.

Rules every line follows:
- Second person ("you"), present tense. Never use any name, never the word {name}; the line is for whoever walks up, any hero.
- One or two sentences, under about 30 words in all. The second sentence is usually the turn or the payoff.
- Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a temperature) over adjectives. No game words (no HP, roll, check, level, search, DC, saving throw, class names). Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No modern slang. No winks at the player.
- No facts the party has not earned: only what a person standing in front of the thing could see, smell, hear or touch. Use only the facts given for each key; do not invent new people, places, monsters, props, objects or history. Do not name any real-world place.
- Drop a final g ("hangin'", "creakin'") in about one line in three, not more, and use no other dialect spelling (reckon, ain't and folks are fine, sparingly). The fiddle is never written or mentioned.
- Plain punctuation only: commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, quotation marks. No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no backticks, no stage directions, no placeholders other than where a key below says an EXTRA line may use {name}.
- Do not repeat an image in neighbouring keys. The house's palette, to spread across the lines, one or two details per line, not all at once: sepia rot and mildew green, faded rose and teal wallpaper, bruised purple upholstery, cracked tile, cobweb grey, dust and mildew; nothing square (doors that are trapezoids, frames that lean, floors that slope, a bulging turret); weasels scratching inside every wall; teeth clicking underfoot; a clock ticking somewhere; the storm; windows sealed and black, streaked with rain, lit by lightning. Sweet rot is the smell of the dining room only, burnt flesh the smell of the kitchen only, copper the smell of the bathroom only. The rooms are unlit unless the party brings light.

Output format, nothing else: for each key, a block exactly like

KEY enter:h2_foyer
PLAIN: the line
PLAIN2: a second plain line (only when the key says so)
EXTRA [class:bard]: the extra line (only when the key says so; this one may begin with {name} and say what that hero does or notices; it must still make sense alone)

Every key needs its PLAIN line, which must stand alone for any hero.
BATCH B1: EXAMINE LINES (first floor, second floor and the children's room). One block per key, PLAIN only unless an EXTRA is named. Each line says what the thing is and what it implies; the second sentence is the payoff or the unease. Where a key says "the fight begins", the line is the last quiet look before trouble, so let the second sentence tilt toward it without naming a monster or saying what happens next.

KEY examine:h1_porch_edge
Facts: where the porch boards end at the rail, with the storm beyond it. Rain slants past the lip, lightning shows only black water falling, and the thunder is overhead.

KEY examine:h2_chandelier
Facts: twenty feet up, hanging tilted, half its crystals gone, thick with dust and cobweb. It sways a little though no draught moves.

KEY examine:h2_stair
Facts: a curved stair climbing to a balcony. The treads are different heights, the runner is bruised purple and worn through, the banister leans.

KEY examine:h3_fireplace
Facts: a cold hearth under cobweb, soot-black, with a mantel of dusty ornaments. A faint smell of old ash. Nothing burns.

KEY examine:h3_crystal_ball
Facts: a glass ball on a brass claw stand on a shelf. It is clouded and cold, and your light does not reach its heart.

KEY examine:h4_peacock
Facts: an oversized albino peacock of white marble in an alcove, tail fanned in stone, one eye a dull red stone. The fight begins when you reach for the red stone, so end on a faint tick or shift in the stone.

KEY examine:h4_bust
Facts: a dour marble bust on a plinth, lips turned down, a small brass plaque below it gone dark with tarnish. Do not say what the plaque says.

KEY examine:h5_mirror
Facts: a tall cracked oval mirror, the silver gone black in spots, one long crack from edge to edge. Your own faces look back, a hair out of step.

KEY examine:h6_table
Facts: the long table and its feast: a sugar bowl, a roast fish, a lobster claw, a pastry, a beef tongue, steam rising straight up. The cloth is spotless though dust lies thick on everything else. The smell is sweet rot. The fight begins when you step to the table, so end on the steam or a plate stirring.

KEY examine:h7_shelf
Facts: a tall metal shelf fallen across the floor, tins and jars burst and rusted, the contents long since turned to black crust. Nothing here is usable.

KEY examine:h8_bergamot
Facts: the one living tree in the glass room, glossy leaves and hard green fruit, among dead brown vines. The bark looks damp, and a sharp citrus smell cuts through the mildew. The rain hammers the glass roof above it.

KEY examine:h8_cup
Facts: a porcelain cup, thin as an eggshell with a hair-line gold rim, on a saucer. The tea in it is dark and steams, though nothing in the room is warm.

KEY examine:h9_clock
Facts: a grandfather clock, case leaning away from the wall, glass door cracked, brass pendulum swinging. The tick is slow and louder than it ought to be, and the hands read no hour that makes sense. The fight begins as you open it, so end on something small stirring inside the case. EXTRA [class:wizard]: starts with {name}.

KEY examine:h9_rail
Facts: the cracked rail of the sitting room, looking down over the foyer twenty feet below. A split in the wood, the portraits' eyes turned up toward you, the tilted chandelier at eye level.

KEY examine:h10_closet
Facts: a closet door standing ajar, small coats and a school cap hanging in the dark, a smell of old wool.

KEY examine:h10_bed_left
Facts: the left of two small beds beside the dark window, blanket rumpled, a deep dust in the dip of the pillow, the dark beneath the bed deeper than it should be.

KEY examine:h10_bed_right
Facts: the right of two small beds beside the dark window, blanket pulled tight and square, a single cloth doll's shoe on the pillow, the dark beneath the bed deeper than it should be. (The doll's shoe is a real detail; no doll is visible.)

KEY examine:h10_chest
Facts: a big toy chest with a heavy lid, painted animals flaking off the sides, a brass hasp. Something inside shifts a little each time the house creaks.

KEY examine:h10_armoire
Facts: a child's armoire carved with stars, its two doors not quite meeting, a thin line of black between them.

KEY examine:h10_window
Facts: a small window sealed shut, black glass streaked with rain, lightning making your own reflections jump. There is no outside to see.
result:
KEY examine:h1_porch_edge
PLAIN: The porch boards end at the rail where rain slants past the lip. Lightning shows only black water fallin' while thunder sits dead overhead.

KEY examine:h2_chandelier
PLAIN: Twenty feet up, it hangs tilted with half its crystals gone, thick with dust and cobweb grey. There ain't a breath of wind, yet it sways.

KEY examine:h2_stair
PLAIN: A curved stair climbs toward the balcony under a worn runner of bruised purple. No two treads match in height, and the banister leans out.

KEY examine:h3_fireplace
PLAIN: Soot-black stone sits cold under cobweb and a mantel of dusty ornaments. You catch the dry smell of old ash, though nothing burns here now.

KEY examine:h3_crystal_ball
PLAIN: A clouded glass ball rests on a brass claw stand, cold to the touch. You hold your light close, and the glow dies before reachin' its heart.

KEY examine:h4_peacock
PLAIN: An oversized peacock of white marble fills the alcove, its stone tail fanned wide around one dull red eye. As you reach out, something in the marble gives a faint click.

KEY examine:h4_bust
PLAIN: A dour marble face looks down from its plinth, stone lips turned sour. Below it sits a small brass plaque gone black with tarnish.

KEY examine:h5_mirror
PLAIN: One long crack splits the tall oval glass where the silver backing has rotted black. Your own faces look back at you, a hair out of step.

KEY examine:h6_table
PLAIN: Roast fish, a beef tongue, a lobster claw, and a sugar bowl sit on a spotless cloth, thick with the smell of sweet rot. Steam rises straight up as a plate gives a slow rattle.

KEY examine:h7_shelf
PLAIN: The tall metal shelf lies fallen across the floor among burst tins and rusted jars. Whatever they held has long since turned to black crust.

KEY examine:h8_bergamot
PLAIN: Rain hammers the glass roof above one living tree with damp bark and hard green fruit among dead brown vines. Its sharp citrus smell cuts right through the mildew.

KEY examine:h8_cup
PLAIN: The porcelain cup is thin as an eggshell on its saucer, traced with a hairline rim of gold. The room is stone cold, yet the dark tea inside still steams.

KEY examine:h9_clock
PLAIN: The grandfather clock leans out from the wall, its brass pendulum swingin' behind cracked glass to an hour that makes no sense. That slow tick is too loud, and something small stirs inside the case.
EXTRA [class:wizard]: {name} studies the wrong-way hands while something inside the leaning case shifts against the wood.

KEY examine:h9_rail
PLAIN: The sitting room rail is split right through, twenty feet above the foyer floor. The tilted chandelier hangs at eye height, and the painted eyes in the portraits all turn up toward you.

KEY examine:h10_closet
PLAIN: The closet door stands ajar on a smell of old wool. Small coats and a school cap hang waitin' in the dark.

KEY examine:h10_bed_left
PLAIN: Beside the dark window, the left bed sits with its blanket rumpled and deep dust settled in the dip of the pillow. Beneath the frame, the dark lies thicker than it ought to.

KEY examine:h10_bed_right
PLAIN: The blanket on the right-hand bed is pulled tight, with a single cloth shoe from a doll resting on the pillow. Underneath, the black goes down too deep for a floor.

KEY examine:h10_chest
PLAIN: Painted animals flake off the sides of the heavy toy chest behind its brass hasp. Every time the house creaks, something inside shifts its weight.

KEY examine:h10_armoire
PLAIN: Stars are carved across the face of the child's armoire. Its two doors hang crooked, leavin' a thin line of black between them.

KEY examine:h10_window
PLAIN: Rain streaks the black glass of a small window sealed tight against the storm. There is no outside to see, only lightning making your own reflections jump.
